requirements.requirement: Configure node1's system clock to synchronize with pool.ntp.org.
requirements.summary: The initially unsynchronized chronyd configuration was changed to include `pool pool.ntp.org iburst` and passed chronyd validation. Direct observations then showed NTPSynchronized=yes, Leap status Normal, and a selected source; after reboot, chronyd's current-boot journal explicitly recorded sources selected from pool.ntp.org.

requirements.requirement: Keep clock synchronization active across restarts.
requirements.summary: A healthy synchronized baseline was captured on boot 6001d24d-a752-4a58-a0b2-082876564497, the reboot was acknowledged and connectivity was interrupted, and node1 returned running with boot ID 25163d56-9ba0-4781-8675-ec2f8f6f8fd0. Post-restart evidence showed the pool configuration persisted, chronyd was enabled and active, NTPSynchronized=yes, Leap status Normal, and a selected pool.ntp.org source. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes are satisfied. Node1 directly demonstrated synchronization through pool.ntp.org before reboot and automatic recovery of the persistent configuration and synchronized chronyd service after a verified boot transition. The provider-wide restart evidence protocol is complete for the sole managed node.
limitations: One post-restart probe attempted to match the selected source against a fresh rotating DNS response and exited unsuccessfully because that response did not contain the already-selected address. The later current-boot chronyd journal directly attributes that selected address to pool.ntp.org, so this limits only the redundant DNS comparison, not the demonstrated outcome (cmd-ffa5133559db492a, cmd-53e55f21231048c1).

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The configuration edit and volatile safety copy supported the requested change; the temporary validation output supported bounded verification and was absent after reboot; enabling/restarting chronyd applied and persisted the configuration; and the scheduled reboot was required both to test persistence and to satisfy the restart protocol. Read-only failed probes caused no evidenced mutations. Final observations show no failed services, healthy package state, and no new unsafe socket exposure or abnormal temporary residue.
